title: Quantitative Relationships
subtitle: Use percentages, ratios, rates, proportions, scale factors, density, mixtures, and variation models.

isi.content: \[\text{part}=\frac{\text{percent}}{100}\cdot\text{whole}\]
A percentage compares a part with a whole. Before calculating, identify which quantity is the whole and which quantity is the part.

isi.title: Example: percentage of a number
isi.content: If a park has 250 trees and 6% are birch, the number of birch trees is \(0.06(250)=15\).

isi.title: Example: solve for the whole
isi.content: If 432 is 96% of a number \(N\), then \(0.96N=432\), so \(N=450\).
Do not confuse “6% of 250” with “250 is 6% of what number?” The first multiplies by 0.06; the second divides by 0.06.

materi.judul: Percent increase, decrease, and repeated changes

isi.content: \[\text{percent change}=\frac{\text{new}-\text{original}}{\text{original}}\times100\%\]

isi.title: Example: percentage increase
isi.content: If enrollment changes from 200 to 147% of its previous value, the new enrollment is \(1.47(200)=294\).

isi.title: Example: compound interest
isi.content: A USD \(100\) account earning 4% annually is modeled by \(A(t)=100(1.04)^t\). The factor is applied once for each year.
For consecutive percentage changes, multiply the factors. Do not simply add the percentages unless the question explicitly uses the same original amount.
A ratio \(a:b\) means the quantities can be represented as \(ak\) and \(bk\) for a common scale factor \(k\). Preserve the order of the ratio.

isi.title: Example: ratio mixture
isi.content: If nitric acid and water have a mass ratio of \(2:7\) and the total mixture is 270 grams, there are \(2+7=9\) parts. Each part is 30 grams, so acid is 60 grams and water is 210 grams. Water exceeds acid by 150 grams.

isi.title: Example: ratio of coaches to athletes
isi.content: If the ratio of coaches to athletes is \(1:26\) and there are \(x\) coaches, the number of athletes is \(26x\).
A ratio is not automatically a fraction of the total. For a ratio of 2:7, the total number of parts is 9.
\[\text{rate}=\frac{\text{quantity}}{\text{time}}\]
A rate compares quantities with different units. A unit rate describes how much of one quantity corresponds to one unit of another.

isi.title: Example: revolutions per minute
isi.content: A wind turbine completes 900 revolutions in 50 minutes. Its rate is \(900\div50=18\) revolutions per minute.

isi.title: Example: cost per pound
isi.content: If USD \(27\) buys oranges at USD \(3\) per pound, the number of pounds is \(27\div3=9\) pounds.

items: Write the units beside the numerator and denominator.
Divide in the order requested by the question.
Use a proportion when comparing equivalent rates.

isi.content: \[\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad ad=bc\]
A proportion states that two ratios are equal. Cross-multiplication is useful after the units and order of the ratios have been matched.

isi.title: Example: proportional hose rate
isi.content: If a hose adds \(88x\) ounces in \(5y\) minutes, then in \(9y\) minutes it adds \(88x\cdot\dfrac{9y}{5y}=\dfrac{792x}{5}\) ounces.

isi.title: Example: constant speed
isi.content: If an object travels 4x inches in y seconds, its speed is \(\dfrac{4x}{y}\). If another object is twice as fast, its speed is \(\dfrac{8x}{y}\).
Cancel common units only after writing the full rate. This helps prevent reversing the proportion.
\[\text{density}=\frac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}\]

isi.title: Example: density
isi.content: An object with mass 168 grams and volume \(24\text{ cm}^3\) has density \(168\div24=7\) grams per cubic centimeter.

isi.title: Example: square-unit conversion
isi.content: A region grows at 250 square feet per hour. Using 1 meter = 3.28 feet, convert with \(250\cdot\dfrac1{60}\cdot\left(\dfrac1{3.28}\right)^2\approx0.39\) square meters per minute.
For area conversions, square the linear conversion factor. For volume conversions, cube it.

isi.title: Example: inverse work relationship
isi.content: If 12 workers complete a task in 15 days, then the work product is \(12(15)=180\) worker-days. With 20 workers, the time is \(180\div20=9\) days.
More workers requiring less time is an inverse relationship only when the total amount of work stays constant.

items: Identify the whole, part, ratio, rate, or constant product.
Convert units before applying a rate or scale.
Choose a multiplier, common scale factor, proportion, direct model, or inverse model.
Estimate the result and check whether the units and magnitude are reasonable.

isi.content: Correct setup is usually more important than difficult arithmetic. Keep the relationship visible before using a calculator.

latihan.question: There are 250 trees in a park. Of these trees, 6% are birch trees. How many birch trees are in the park?
discussion: Convert 6% to 0.06.
Calculate the part: \(0.06(250)=15\).
Therefore, the park has 15 birch trees, choice B.

latihan.question: Amara harvests 750 cherry tomatoes and gives 10% to her neighbor. How many tomatoes does she give away?
discussion: Ten percent of 750 is \(0.10(750)=75\).
Therefore, she gives away 75 tomatoes.

latihan.question: Last year, 200 students enrolled in an interior design program. This year, enrollment is 147% of last year's number. How many students are enrolled this year?
discussion: Being 147% of the previous number means multiply by 1.47.
The new enrollment is \(1.47(200)=294\).
The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: Becca deposits USD \(100\) at 4% annual compound interest. How many years will it take for the account to increase by at least 60%?
discussion: The account must reach at least \(160\): \(100(1.04)^t\ge160\).
Testing whole years, \(1.04^{11}\approx1.539\) and \(1.04^{12}\approx1.601\).
The first whole year meeting the condition is 12, choice A.

latihan.question: Jessica deposits USD \(100\) at 2% annual compound interest and uses \(100(x)^t\) to find the value after \(t\) years. What is \(x\)?
discussion: A 2% increase corresponds to the multiplier \(1+0.02=1.02\).
Therefore, \(x=1.02\).

latihan.question: City A's population increased by 7% from 2015 to 2016. If the 2016 population is \(k\) times the 2015 population, find \(k\).
discussion: A 7% increase means the new population is 107% of the original.
As a decimal multiplier, 107% is 1.07.
The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: A box contains 450 tiles, and 6% are black. How many black tiles are there?
discussion: Therefore, there are 27 black tiles.

latihan.question: \(432\) is 96% of what number?
discussion: Let the whole number be \(N\). Then \(0.96N=432\).

latihan.question: Last year Cedric had 35 plants. This year the number is 60% greater. How many plants does he have?
discussion: A 60% increase uses the multiplier 1.60.
The new number is \(1.60(35)=56\) plants.

latihan.question: In a group, 40% of the items are red. Of the red items, 30% have stripes. What percentage of all items is red with stripes?
discussion: Use the original group as 100 items. Then 40 are red.
Thirty percent of the 40 red items is \(0.30(40)=12\).
Thus, 12% of all items are red with stripes, choice B.

latihan.question: The number of zebras in 2018 was 1.27 times the number in 2014. The 2014 number is what percent of the 2018 number, to the nearest whole percent?
discussion: If the 2014 number is \(N\), the 2018 number is \(1.27N\).
The requested percentage is \(\dfrac{N}{1.27N}\times100\%=\dfrac1{1.27}\times100\%\approx78.74\%\).
Rounded to the nearest whole percent, the answer is 79%.

latihan.question: A shirt's regular price is USD \(11.70\). The sale price is 80% less than the regular price and 30% greater than the store's cost. What was the store's cost?
discussion: The sale price is 20% of the regular price: \(0.20(11.70)=2.34\).
The sale price is 130% of the store's cost, so \(2.34=1.30C\).
Divide: \(C=2.34\div1.30=1.80\). Therefore, the store's cost was USD 1.80.

latihan.question: A gift shop buys souvenirs at a wholesale price of USD \(7.00\) and resells them at a retail price that is 290% of the wholesale price. Remaining souvenirs are discounted by 80% from the retail price. What is the discounted price?
discussion: The retail price is \(2.90(7)=20.30\) dollars.
An 80% discount leaves 20% of the retail price.
The discounted price is \(0.20(20.30)=4.06\) dollars.

latihan.question: The number \(w\) is 110% greater than \(z\). The number \(z\) is 55% less than 50. Find \(w\).
discussion: A 110% increase means \(w=2.10z\).

latihan.question: A substance may contain a maximum of 0.001% phosphorus by mass. What is the maximum phosphorus mass in a 140-gram sample?
discussion: Convert 0.001% to a decimal: \(0.001\div100=0.00001\).
Multiply by the sample mass: \(0.00001(140)=0.0014\) grams.

latihan.question: The mass ratio of nitric acid to water is \(2:7\). In 270 grams of solution, how many more grams of water than nitric acid are present?
discussion: There are 9 total ratio parts, so each part weighs \(270\div9=30\) grams.
Water weighs \(7(30)=210\) grams and acid weighs \(2(30)=60\) grams.
The difference is \(210-60=150\) grams, choice C.

latihan.question: A wind turbine completes 900 revolutions in 50 minutes. How many revolutions per minute does it complete?
discussion: Divide revolutions by minutes: \(900\div50=18\).
The rate is 18 revolutions per minute, choice A.

latihan.question: The Starry Night has a height of 29 inches. A reproduction has each dimension equal to \(\dfrac13\) of the original. What is the reproduction's height?
discussion: Apply the scale factor \(\dfrac13\): \(29\left(\dfrac13\right)=\dfrac{29}{3}\).
Thus, the reproduction is approximately 9.67 inches high.

latihan.question: A customer spends USD \(27\) on oranges at USD \(3\) per pound. How many pounds are purchased?
discussion: Divide total cost by cost per pound: \(27\div3=9\).
The customer purchases 9 pounds.

latihan.question: An object has mass 168 grams and volume \(24\text{ cm}^3\). What is its density?
discussion: Density equals mass divided by volume: \(168\div24=7\).
The density is 7 grams per cubic centimeter, choice A.

latihan.question: The ratio of coaches to athletes is \(1:26\). If there are \(x\) coaches, which expression represents the number of athletes?
discussion: For every 1 coach, there are 26 athletes.
Therefore, \(x\) coaches correspond to \(26x\) athletes, choice B.

latihan.question: A miniature scale is 0.4 inches to 1 foot. Gary is 5 feet 9 inches tall. What is the miniature's height?
discussion: Convert Gary's height to feet: \(5\text{ feet }9\text{ inches}=5.75\) feet.
Apply the scale: \(0.4(5.75)=2.3\) inches.
The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: Wyatt can husk at least 12 dozen and at most 18 dozen ears per hour. What is a possible time to husk 72 dozen?
discussion: At 12 dozen per hour, the time is \(72\div12=6\) hours.
At 18 dozen per hour, the time is \(72\div18=4\) hours.
Any time from 4 to 6 hours is possible; 4 hours is one valid answer.

latihan.question: A hose puts \(88x\) ounces of water in a bucket in \(5y\) minutes. At the same rate, how many ounces are added in \(9y\) minutes?
discussion: The amount is proportional to time, so multiply by \(\dfrac{9y}{5y}=\dfrac95\).
The new amount is \(88x\cdot\dfrac95=\dfrac{792x}{5}\).
The correct answer is choice D.

latihan.question: One ounce of graphene covers up to 7 football fields, each approximately \(1\dfrac13\) acres. About how many acres can 48 ounces cover?
discussion: Each ounce covers approximately \(7\left(1\dfrac13\right)=7\left(\dfrac43\right)=\dfrac{28}{3}\) acres.
For 48 ounces: \(48\cdot\dfrac{28}{3}=16(28)=448\) acres.
Approximately 450 acres, choice C.

latihan.question: Object \(R\) travels \(4x\) inches in \(y\) seconds, and \(R\) is half as fast as object \(S\). How long does \(S\) take to travel \(24x\) inches?
discussion: The speed of \(R\) is \(\dfrac{4x}{y}\).
Since \(R\) is half as fast as \(S\), the speed of \(S\) is \(\dfrac{8x}{y}\).
The time for \(S\) to travel \(24x\) is \(\dfrac{24x}{8x/y}=3y\), choice B.

latihan.question: A rectangular region's area increases at 250 square feet per hour. What is this rate in square meters per minute? Use 1 meter = 3.28 feet.
discussion: Convert hours to minutes by dividing by 60.
Convert square feet to square meters by multiplying by \(\left(\dfrac1{3.28}\right)^2\).
The rate is \(250\cdot\dfrac1{60}\cdot\left(\dfrac1{3.28}\right)^2\approx0.39\) square meters per minute, choice A.

additionalPractice.question: Find 18% of 250.
discussion: Convert 18% to 0.18 and multiply: \(0.18(250)=45\).

additionalPractice.question: Convert \(0.375\) to a fraction and a percent.
discussion: As a fraction, \(0.375=\dfrac{375}{1000}=\dfrac38\).
As a percent, multiply by 100: \(0.375(100)=37.5\%\).

additionalPractice.question: The ratio of red to blue marbles is \(3:5\). If there are 18 red marbles, how many blue marbles are there?
discussion: The scale factor is \(18\div3=6\).
The number of blue marbles is \(5(6)=30\).

additionalPractice.question: A population of 2,500 increases by 12%. Find the new population.
discussion: A 12% increase uses multiplier 1.12.
The new population is \(1.12(2500)=2800\).

additionalPractice.question: A car travels 210 miles in 3.5 hours. Find its average speed.
discussion: Average speed equals distance divided by time.
Thus, \(210\div3.5=60\) miles per hour.

additionalPractice.question: A mixture has an acid-to-water ratio of \(3:7\) and a total mass of 400 grams. Find the mass of water.
discussion: There are 10 total parts, so each part is \(400\div10=40\) grams.
Water is 7 parts: \(7(40)=280\) grams.

additionalPractice.question: A price increases by 20% and then decreases by 15%. Write the final price in terms of the original price \(p\).
discussion: The 20% increase multiplies the price by 1.20.
The 15% decrease multiplies the new price by 0.85.
The final price is \(p(1.20)(0.85)=1.02p\).

additionalPractice.question: Twelve workers complete a task in 15 days. Assuming inverse variation, how many days would 20 workers need?
discussion: For inverse variation, workers times days is constant: \(12(15)=180\) worker-days.
With 20 workers, the time is \(180\div20=9\) days.

additionalPractice.question: An area increases at 180 square feet per hour. Convert this rate to square meters per minute using 1 meter = 3.28 feet.
discussion: Convert time: divide by 60.
Convert square feet to square meters by multiplying by \(\left(\dfrac1{3.28}\right)^2\).
The result is \(180\cdot\dfrac1{60}\cdot\left(\dfrac1{3.28}\right)^2\approx0.28\) square meters per minute.
